questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Introduction to Structural Steel & Limit State Design Concepts
questions.text: Explain Limit State Design philosophy of steel connections according to IS 800:2007. Derive formulas for: (a) Shear capacity of bolt ($V_{dsb} = \frac{f_{ub}}{\sqrt{3}\gamma_{mb}}(n_n A_{nb} + n_s A_{sb})$), (b) Bearing capacity ($V_{dpb} = \frac{2.5 k_b d t f_u}{\gamma_{mb}}$), and (c) Tensile capacity of bolts ($T_{db}$). Design a double cover butt joint to connect two plates of $16\,\text{mm}$ thickness carrying a factored axial tension of $400\,\text{kN}$ using grade 4.6 bolts and Fe410 steel.

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Introduction to Structural Steel & Limit State Design Concepts
questions.text: Design a Fillet Weld connection to connect a tie member consisting of an ISA $100 \times 75 \times 8\,\text{mm}$ to a $10\,\text{mm}$ thick gusset plate to carry a factored tensile force of $250\,\text{kN}$. Design side welds along top and bottom edges of the angle such that the centroid of weld group coincides with the centroid of the angle section.

questions.chapter: Chapter 3: Design of Tension Members & Lug Angles
questions.text: Explain Shear Lag effect in angle tension members. State the design strength equations for tension members according to IS 800:2007: (a) Gross section yielding $T_{dg} = \frac{A_g f_y}{\gamma_{m0}}$, (b) Net section rupture $T_{dn} = \frac{0.9 A_{nc} f_u}{\gamma_{m1}} + \frac{\beta A_o f_y}{\gamma_{m0}}$, and (c) Block Shear strength ($T_{db1}, T_{db2}$). Design a single angle tension member to carry a factored tensile force of $220\,\text{kN}$.

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Introduction to Structural Steel & Limit State Design Concepts
questions.text: Explain the Column Buckling Curves (Classes a, b, c, d) and Perry-Robertson formula for design compressive strength $f_{cd} = \frac{f_y / \gamma_{m0}}{\phi + [\phi^2 - \lambda^2]^{0.5}}$ according to IS 800:2007. Design a single rolled steel column section (ISHB 300 / ISMB 400) of effective length $4.0\,\text{m}$ to support a factored axial load of $1200\,\text{kN}$.

questions.chapter: Chapter 4: Design of Compression Members & Built-Up Columns
questions.text: Design a Built-Up Column consisting of two channel sections placed face-to-face / back-to-back to carry a factored axial compressive load of $1500\,\text{kN}$ over an effective length of $6.0\,\text{m}$. Design a Single Lacing System for the column with connection details conforming to IS 800:2007 (Transverse shear $V_t = 2.5\% P$).

questions.chapter: Chapter 5: Design of Laterally Supported & Unsupported Steel Beams
questions.text: Explain the design steps for a Laterally Supported Beam according to IS 800:2007: (a) Section classification (Plastic, Compact, Semi-compact), (b) Design bending strength $M_d = \beta_b Z_p \frac{f_y}{\gamma_{m0}} \le 1.2 Z_e \frac{f_y}{\gamma_{m0}}$, (c) Design shear strength $V_d = \frac{A_v f_y}{\sqrt{3}\gamma_{m0}}$, (d) Web buckling and web crippling checks, (e) Deflection check ($\delta \le L/300$). Design a simply supported beam of span $6\,\text{m}$ carrying a live load of $20\,\text{kN/m}$.

questions.chapter: Chapter 6: Design of Column Bases & Roof Trusses
questions.text: Design a Slab Base for an ISHB 350 column carrying a factored axial compressive load of $1400\,\text{kN}$. The base plate rests on an M20 grade concrete foundation pedestal with safe bearing capacity of soil $= 200\,\text{kN/m}^2$. Calculate plate thickness $t_s = \sqrt{\frac{2.5 w(a^2 - 0.3b^2)\gamma_{m0}}{f_y}}$ and design holding down anchor bolts.

Design a Battened Column consisting of two ISMC 300 channels to carry a factored load of $1000\,\text{kN}$ over an effective length of $5\,\text{m}$. Design intermediate and end battens with bolt connections.
